steps.title: Telemetry, web UI, heartbeat and e-stop
steps.note: Full stack verified: agent on UDP 8888, all 4 nodes up, 17 topics in the /gps_localize namespace, heartbeat publishing at 10.1 Hz, e-stop accepting commands, web UI 200 on every asset. Only the physical ESP32 is missing.

steps.title: Navigation and the rest of the graph
steps.note: Firmware now scans and joins the strongest listed Wi-Fi, so changing network needs no reflash. Remaining: install the systemd unit (needs sudo) and 6 pre-existing estimator/motor-model test failures.

log.what: Telemetry is now gps_localize_msgs/Telemetry with 44 named fields, verified on the real board at 7.4 Hz with every value correct for a bare ESP32. The web UI needed zero changes because it already read by name. Four traps on the way, all now guarded by QC: micro-ROS skips its entire build if libmicroros.a exists, so nothing took effect until that was deleted; a symlink in extra_packages is not followed since the builder copies directories; lifting the fault-bitfield assignment out of the packed-array code left its local variable undeclared; and port_qc took whichever package.xml sorted first, so with two packages it tested the message package and complained it had no setup.py.

Moving telemetry from a packed 44-float array to a named gps_localize_msgs/Telemetry, on your call that ROS 2 stays and should be easy to extend. The array was the exact 'hard to edit' pattern the UDP question was about, living inside ROS: adding a signal meant keeping an index in step across three files. Now it is one line in the .msg. The web UI needed no change at all - it already read fields by name. The .msg was generated from telemetry.py's FIELDS so the names matched at birth, and QC now checks the two copies stay identical, that every declared field is actually assigned (an unset field would publish a silent zero rather than fail), and that no node still subscribes to the old type. telemetry.py still accepts the old array so recorded bags replay.

The robot is on the ROS graph over Wi-Fi: /gps_localize_firmware with all 10 contract topics and telemetry at 8 Hz. mDNS found the PC by name (mannaja.local -> 10.94.163.220) rather than the stale hardcoded IP, which is exactly what that resolution chain was built for. Two more real bugs on the way: the IMU driver crashed the board when its sensor was absent, and QC check 14 used 'ros2 topic hz', which never exits, so it always timed out and claimed telemetry had stopped while the board published at 8 Hz - it had only looked correct because it skipped without hardware. Full port QC now passes 14/14 with hardware in the loop.

First flash onto the real ESP32. It boots, degrades gracefully with no sensors attached (IMU, INA226 and compass all report missing and it carries on), and the Wi-Fi scan works - 17 to 18 APs found. Two real bugs came out of it that no simulation would have produced: the board rebooted forever when no configured network was in range, which makes it impossible to configure; and the scan gave no clue what WAS in range. Both fixed. Learned from the scan list that the PC is on a 5 GHz radio the ESP32 cannot see.
log.problem: no 2.4 GHz network configured that reaches the PC

log.what: Docker works end to end: image builds, stack comes up healthy, web UI serves, 19 topics visible. Getting there found six separate causes, every one a real defect rather than a tweak - the agent could not be built from source at all (three different dead ends, now micro_ros_setup), rosdep needed apt lists, my rewrite had deleted the apt layer taking pip and curl, rosdep could not resolve micro_ros_agent, the container refused to start because /dev/ttyUSB0 was absent, and docker exec had no ros2 because exec skips the entrypoint. The device one matters most: it meant the stack could not start on any machine without the robot plugged in, which is the normal case.

Position EKF landed. GPS now corrects position instead of it being open-loop dead reckoning. Measurement variance comes from the receiver's own hdop and fix quality, so an RTK receiver improves the result with no code change, and outlier gating stops a multipath jump yanking the estimate - while still giving in after five rejections so it cannot sit stale and confident. Seven tests measured against known truth; two failed first and both were my tests rather than the filter, which is recorded in the file. 139 host tests pass.

Built the simulation harness the EKF depends on. SimWorld integrates a true pose from commanded wheel speeds and synthesises each sensor from it with realistic error - GPS at 1 Hz with 2 m noise and dropouts, IMU with a drifting gyro bias, compass with a hard-iron offset, INA226 values consistent with the PWM. Because the truth is known, the eight new tests measure error rather than assert behaviour. Checked they can actually fail by tightening two bounds to absurd values and confirming both broke; that also measured current heading accuracy at 0.375 degrees after 20 s of driving with bias. 132 host tests pass.

Docker build: four distinct causes found and fixed so far. The agent could not be built from source at all (superbuild has no install target; without it microxrcedds_client is missing; with it the pinned FastDDS tag no longer exists upstream), so it now uses micro_ros_setup, the supported route and the same one that produced the agent on this machine. rosdep then failed because the apt lists had been cleared. Then pip3 was missing because my rewrite of that block had deleted the apt layer above it, which also took curl - which the healthcheck needs.

New standing priority from you: finish everything on THIS Ubuntu first, leave cross-platform work until after. Windows tasks stay in the plan but move behind the Ubuntu ones. Your Windows run found a real bug already - the viewer reported 'No module named configstore' when the actual problem was a missing pyyaml, because a broad except swallowed it. Fixed and verified by reproducing it here.

Traced the sudo block to the snap build of VS Code, not to Claude Code: the first process in the chain with NoNewPrivs=1 was the snap, its parent systemd --user had 0, and Seccomp was 0 throughout. Reinstalling VS Code from the .deb cleared it. Then ran the real installer, which built the workspace and installed the systemd unit - verified the service is enabled, active, owns port 8080 in its own cgroup, and serves 19 topics. Docker installed.

Sudoers file installed and correct (root:root, 0440), but it does not help me: this shell has NoNewPrivs set, which blocks sudo at the kernel level whatever sudoers allows. Checked rootless Docker as a way around it - it needs newuidmap/newgidmap from the uidmap package, so that needs root too. Anything requiring root now has to be run in your terminal.
log.problem: NoNewPrivs=1 blocks sudo for the assistant

log.what: Topics tab and compass rose added. The tab lists every topic with type, publisher and subscriber counts and measured rate, filters, and expands any topic to show its live value - the robot subscribes on demand and drops it again when the page stops asking. The map gained a compass rose: north, a solid needle for the fused heading the robot steers by, a hollow one for the raw QMC5883 when a healthy compass is fitted, and the heading source underneath. When the needles separate the magnetometer is being disturbed, which is the moment you want to see it. The Windows viewer serves both endpoints with simulated data so the page never 404s there, which QC enforces. Also added a JavaScript parse check to QC - nothing else would have caught a broken app.js: Python compiles, firmware builds, QC passes, and the page is simply dead when opened.
log.files: web_server.py, viewer_server.py, web/index.html, web/app.js, web/style.css, tools/qc.py

log.what: Topics API added so the whole ROS graph is visible from a browser. There is no ros2 CLI on Windows or inside Docker Desktop, so /api/topics lists every topic with its type, publisher and subscriber counts and measured rate, and /api/topic subscribes on demand and returns the live value. Subscriptions are reaped once nobody is polling, so opening the page does not leave them behind. Verified: 16 topics enumerated, live echo of std_msgs/String at a measured 5.0 Hz, unknown topic refused cleanly.

All six failing host tests resolved by cause, not by adjusting expectations. Two were real firmware bugs: the estimator's anti-creep floor trapped the speed estimate at zero forever (the robot would have read 0 m/s at low speed, which is exactly what the waypoint controller relies on), and that same bug was why the GPS-course test failed - speed never exceeded align_min_mps. The PIDF deadband left d_init set, so the first D kick after a setpoint step went through unfiltered. Two were wrong test data: 2.0 A at 12 V through 5 ohm leaves 12.9 rpm of back-EMF and is not a stall, and the model-fallback test ran two time constants against a tolerance needing four. 124/124 pass.

Power sensing corrected to match the wiring, closing the blocker. Pack voltage now comes from the motor rails; the processor INA226 is reported as the ESP32 rail plus module current, which is what it actually measures. A new lib/power/power_monitor.h keeps that mapping in one place instead of spread through main.cpp. Telemetry grew to 42 fields, tiers retiered for 3S, diode drops set to your measured 1.81/1.90 V.
log.files: power_monitor.h, power.h, motor.h, safety_manager.h, main.cpp, telemetry.py

log.what: Added the task board to plan.html: 66 tasks with phase, hardware needed, state, files, the test that proves each one, and its last result. A 'waiting on hardware' panel above it groups the blocked tasks by the part they need.

Removed _backup/ and tools/snapshot.sh. _patches already stores a full before/after per change with a diff and a rollback, and git now covers whole-tree restore, so keeping both was storing the same thing twice. Repairing the plan state afterwards showed why blunt tools are risky: a sed on the JSON stripped a line out of two log entries and broke the generator. Restored by hand.
log.problem: A sed -i '/snapshot/d' on a JSON file removed real content. Fixed; use a JSON-aware edit next time.

log.what: Untracked the exported schematics, the PNG zip and .claude/ at your request, and fixed the two QC failures that exposed. tools/qc.py was treating network_secrets.h as a header config.h must include; it is pulled in by network.h instead. port_qc.py's drive-letter pattern matched any word ending in a colon plus slash, including the docker volume mapping - tightening it then found two places the old pattern had missed, both legitimate, so markdown is now exempt and code can opt out explicitly.

Published the three derived branches from main via git worktrees and rsync --delete. workspace has no firmware, firmware has no ROS workspace or web UI, docker adds a Dockerfile, compose file and one-command installer. The script is idempotent: a second run made no commit on any branch.
Initial commit and push to MechcodeRobotech/ROS_GPS_CAR as Mannaja78520. 106 files. No CAD, no mor_luam, no Wi-Fi credentials on any branch.

Wi-Fi credentials split out of network.h into a gitignored network_secrets.h, with network_secrets.example.h as the committed template. Verified both ways: the firmware builds with the header present, and without it the build stops on a clear #error telling you to copy the example.

Restored the 162 CAD files from the Windows share - all of them were 0 bytes locally, wiped along with everything else and not covered by the earlier restore. Removed mor_luam, which came from a different project. Both verified against the share before and after.

Fixed 8 wrong NMEA checksums in the test fixtures. The coordinates had been changed to Thailand without recomputing the checksum, so the parser was correctly rejecting its own test data. The deliberate bad-checksum test was left corrupt on purpose. Host tests went from 14 failures to 6; every NMEA test now passes.

Added a multi-network Wi-Fi table. On boot the ESP32 scans, keeps the networks that are both visible and listed, and joins the strongest, trying the next if one fails. Changing Wi-Fi is now a one-line edit instead of a reconfigure, and the micro-ROS transport is handed the credentials that actually associated. Builds clean: RAM 24.7%, Flash 47.3%.
Added a timestamped snapshot tool. Later removed in T11 once _patches proved to be the same thing done better, and git history covered the whole-tree case.

Corrected two of my earlier conclusions. mDNS IPv4 does work - avahi-resolve-host-name -4 returns 192.168.100.64; my first check used avahi-resolve -n, which answers IPv6 first. And micro_ros_agent was already installed at ~/uros_ws and sourced from .bashrc, so the agent I built from source was redundant and is now only a fallback.

Full stack verified end to end with one command: ros2 launch gps_localize bringup.launch.py. Agent bound 0.0.0.0:8888, gps_odom / safety_watchdog / waypoint_nav / web_server all came up, 17 topics appeared, heartbeat measured at 10.126 Hz, e-stop accepted a published command, and the web UI returned 200. Everything the host side can do without the robot now works.

Taught bringup.launch.py to use whichever agent exists: the ROS micro_ros_agent package via Node() when installed, otherwise the source-built MicroXRCEAgent binary via ExecuteProcess. The two take different flags (--port/--dev vs -p/-D), so each branch passes its own.

Built the micro-ROS agent from source. ros-humble-micro-ros-agent is not packaged for Humble, so Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent v2.4.2 was compiled against the FastDDS 2.6 that ships with ROS, which guarantees wire compatibility with the ROS 2 graph. Installed to ~/.local/bin, no sudo required.

Fixed a bug my own gate introduced: adding _work to the skip list made find_pkg reject any path containing that name, so pointing the gate at _work/ could no longer find the package. Skip names are now matched relative to the scan root, and the self-check matches by filename so a staged copy of the gate is not linted either.

Pointed the firmware at this machine: AGENT_HOSTNAME ros2-agent -> mannaja, AGENT_IP 192.168.50.242 -> 192.168.100.64, and the unused STATIC_IP block moved to the 192.168.100.x subnet. Fixed the systemd unit, which hardcoded User=ubuntu and /home/ubuntu.

log.files: gps_localize_ws, webapp, tools, setup, docs, firmware
log.what: Took a timestamped snapshot before and after promoting the multi-Wi-Fi and NMEA checksum work.

Fixed a real port bug: the web UI returned 403 on every file. httpd.py checked containment with os.path.realpath, and colcon's --symlink-install links each installed asset back to src/, so every legitimate file resolved outside static_dir and looked like a traversal attempt. Containment is now checked on the normalised path, so '..' is still rejected while symlinked files resolve. Windows never hit this because it has no symlink install.

Merged the two QC suites instead of letting one overwrite the other. The project's own 15 KB cross-file checker keeps the name tools/qc.py; the Ubuntu port gate became tools/port_qc.py. Made the project checker's Windows .exe freshness check platform-aware, since a stale PyInstaller build cannot affect what Linux serves. Both suites now exit 0.
colcon build --symlink-install succeeded on Humble first try, 1.47 s. All 5 nodes (gps_odom, heading_check, safety_watchdog, waypoint_nav, web_server) started and were still alive after 5 s.

Corrected port QC check 11, which was wrong rather than the code. It scanned for literal data[0..39] indexing, but telemetry.py maps a 40-name FIELDS tuple with enumerate, which is the better implementation. The check now parses with ast and accepts a declared length constant, a names sequence, or literal indexing.
Hygiene pass: CRLF stripped from 18 files and the exec bit restored on 11, fanned out across files with xargs -P 6. Port QC went from 5 failures to 1.

Found the complete source at /mnt/winshare/GPS_Localize and copied gps_localize_ws, webapp, docs, setup, tools and firmware into _work/ with six parallel jobs, excluding the 711 MB .pio cache. Their tools/ was staged separately so it could not clobber the new gate.
First QC run against the empty staging tree. Exit 1, promotion blocked, exactly as intended while the source was still missing.

Surveyed the project and recovered the full ROS 2 interface contract from firmware/src/main.cpp: 10 topics, 40 named telemetry fields, config selectors. This became the spec the host side is checked against.

Audited the project for future use. Found five nodes that crashed on the first telemetry frame, a systemd unit that only worked on this machine, a QC check that had gone hollow, a stale Docker image and a stale micro-ROS library. Fixed all of them, added five QC checks, and wrote tools/live_probe.py so hardware-only code paths can be exercised on a bench with no hardware.
log.files: 5 host nodes, systemd unit, setup/install.sh, tools/qc.py, tools/port_qc.py, tools/live_probe.py

log.what: Finished the audit. Proved the Docker fix from a host with nothing configured - the probe decodes fresh telemetry in the container and ros2 topic echo reads live values off it. Corrected four stale test counts and made the number machine-checked. Restored the native systemd stack and re-probed it clean.
log.files: tools/publish_branches.sh, tools/live_probe.py, tools/qc.py, CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/acceptance.md

log.what: First run on real hardware: ESP32 + relay + four INA226s, no battery. Flashed, joined Wi-Fi, resolved the agent by mDNS and linked - E01, E02 and E03 all pass. Found and fixed an input pull that held the board in e-stop from boot. Confirmed the no-battery case does not latch STOP_BATTERY_LOW, which was the bug that would have stopped the robot on first power-on. Board now reaches IDLE with no stop reasons and live INA readings reach the web UI.

Ran on a real 3S pack with no USB. Pack reads 0 and does not latch because the mushroom is engaged and the relay is open, which is correct. Made the hard cutoff latch until power cycle as asked. Found two mapping problems to settle against the hardware rather than guess: the relay sense appears to be on IO13 rather than IO14, and the processor INA is at 0x41 where power.h expects motor A.

Found that the firmware never drove the relay: IO14 was an input in the config and no relay output existed anywhere. Corrected the pin roles to match the built hardware (IO13 mushroom in, IO14 contactor out) and implemented the staged sequence - rails dead through the lockout, close to make the pack measurable, open and stay open on a flat pack.

problems.what: Firmware crashed with Guru Meditation (LoadProhibited) roughly every 15 s: ImuBno085::update() called the Adafruit driver even though begin() had failed, and getSensorEvent() dereferenced uninitialised SHTP state.
problems.state: RESOLVED - update() now returns early when ok_ is false
problems.impact: Not just a bench issue: with an IMU fitted, a loose connector or an I2C fault at boot would have crash-looped the robot instead of degrading it.

problems.what: Firmware rebooted forever when no configured network was in range, making the board impossible to configure - the console never stayed up long enough.
problems.state: RESOLVED - it stays up, retries every 30 s, and lists what it can see
problems.impact: Found only by flashing real hardware; no simulation would have shown it.

problems.what: sudo was blocked for me by NoNewPrivs=1, inherited from the snap-packaged VS Code (snap confines its whole process tree; the flag can never be unset once set). Claude Code was not the cause - Seccomp was 0.
problems.state: RESOLVED - VS Code reinstalled from the .deb, snap removed
problems.impact: Root work is possible again: the systemd service is installed and Docker is in.

problems.what: 6 host tests still fail, in the estimator, motor model and PIDF: derivative filter smoothing, GPS course winning while moving, speed following GPS, speed falling back to the model, and stall detect/clear.
problems.impact: Two were real firmware bugs that would have affected the robot; two were wrong fixtures.

problems.what: The ESP32 has not been reflashed, so it still carries the old single-network Wi-Fi config and AGENT_IP 192.168.50.242.
problems.state: OPEN - PlatformIO is now installed; flash with: cd firmware && pio run -e wifi -t upload
problems.impact: Until it is flashed the robot cannot find the agent. The firmware image is already built and verified.

problems.what: The systemd unit is corrected for this machine but not installed, because copying into /etc/systemd/system needs sudo.
problems.state: OPEN - needs your password, 3 commands in the unit header
problems.impact: The stack does not start on boot yet; ros2 launch works fine by hand.

problems.what: firmware/config/network.h points at the wrong machine. AGENT_HOSTNAME is "ros2-agent" but this host is "mannaja"; AGENT_IP is 192.168.50.242 but this host is 192.168.100.64, a different subnet. WIFI_SSID is "Teelek_IoT" and needs to match the network this PC is on.
problems.impact: Still needs the ESP32 reflashed for the change to reach the robot, and the robot's Wi-Fi must be the same LAN as 192.168.100.0/24.

problems.what: micro_ros_agent was not installed, and ros-humble-micro-ros-agent turned out not to exist in apt for Humble at all.
problems.impact: Solved by building Micro-XRCE-DDS-Agent v2.4.2 against the FastDDS that ships with ROS. No sudo was needed.

problems.what: The entire host-side source was 0 bytes: gps_localize_ws (28 files), webapp (14), docs (8), tools (4), setup (4), and the _backup and _patches archives too.
problems.impact: Was the blocker for the whole port. The likely cause was a failed transfer from the VirtualBox shared folder; copy as an archive rather than a folder sync next time.

problems.what: firmware/platformio.ini was empty, so the ESP32 could not be rebuilt or reflashed.
problems.state: RESOLVED 23:24 - Windows copy had it (3632 bytes), now restored
problems.impact: The firmware can be rebuilt again once PlatformIO is installed.

problems.what: The web UI returned 403 forbidden on every file, including index.html, because httpd.py resolved symlinks before its containment check and colcon's --symlink-install points every installed asset back at src/.
problems.state: RESOLVED 23:31 - containment now checked on the normalised path
problems.impact: Was a genuine Windows-to-Linux port bug; Windows has no symlink install so it never surfaced there. Traversal is still blocked, verified.

problems.what: Five host nodes read msg.data from the named telemetry message and died on every frame. safety_watchdog and waypoint_nav were among them, so the watchdog and the navigator would each have been restarting several times a second while the stack reported healthy.
problems.impact: Invisible without hardware: with no board the callbacks never run, so every other check passed. Found by publishing synthetic telemetry at the running stack.

problems.what: The systemd unit hardcoded User=mannaja and /home/mannaja/GPS_Localize, and install.sh copied it verbatim.
problems.impact: Installing on any other PC produced a service pointing at a user and directory that do not exist. The unit is a template now.

problems.what: Port QC check 11 derived the telemetry width from a #define that no longer exists, got 0, and silently switched off its own telemetry half while still reporting PASS.
problems.impact: A check that verifies nothing is worse than one that fails. It reads the message definition now, and an undeterminable width is a failure rather than a skip.

problems.what: The Docker image predated the named message and contained no gps_localize_msgs; micro_ros_platformio had likewise skipped rebuilding libmicroros for the serial environment.
problems.impact: Both are silent staleness: docker images and pio both reported success. Two freshness checks added, compared against the newest source rather than one file.

problems.what: Host and container completed DDS discovery but exchanged no samples. Fast DDS prefers shared memory once it finds a peer on the same host, and those segments do not cross the container boundary. ipc: host alone did not fix it because the two sides run different Fast DDS builds.
problems.impact: The reassuring kind of failure: ros2 topic list showed all 14 container topics with correct types and subscriber counts, then nothing arrived. Image now pins UDPv4, so a host needs no setup to inspect a containerised stack.

problems.what: tools/live_probe.py reported PASS on telemetry left over from an earlier run, while the frames it had just published were not arriving.
problems.impact: The same hollow-pass fault this audit was created to find, in a tool written during the audit. It now requires the decode to be no older than the run that produced it, and that is what exposed the Docker transport problem.

problems.what: README.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/acceptance.md claimed 120 or 124 host tests; the suite has 139.
problems.impact: Cheapest possible signal that a document has stopped being maintained. The real count is now derived from RUN_TEST calls in the test sources and checked by qc.py.

problems.what: PIN_ESP_EMER_SW is active HIGH but was configured INPUT_PULLUP. With no e-stop button fitted the pin floated high against its own pull, read as permanently pressed, and held STOP_ESP_BUTTON from boot.
problems.impact: The board came up in ESTOP and would never have enabled a motor, with nothing in the log naming the cause. Pulls are now derived from the polarity defines so the two cannot disagree.

problems.what: Switching the PC's Wi-Fi orphaned every running ROS node. DDS binds interfaces at node start, so after the address changed the nodes kept advertising the old one.
problems.impact: ros2 node list came back empty and telemetry subscribers dropped to zero while the topic still existed and the firmware was publishing to it. The web UI served data seven minutes stale. A restart of the unit is the fix.

problems.what: AGENT_IP had gone stale (192.168.100.64 while the machine was on .16), and the comment above it wrongly claimed mDNS could not resolve here.
problems.impact: mDNS does work - the firmware asks for an A record and avahi-resolve -4 answers. Only the IPv6-first default form looks like a failure. The board resolved the agent by mDNS on the first attempt.

problems.what: The hard battery cutoff released itself once the pack recovered above BATT_CUTOFF_CLEAR_V.
problems.impact: A LiPo at the cutoff sags under load and springs back when the load comes off, so the threshold acted as an oscillator: stop, un-latch, drive, sag, stop - draining the cells past damage automatically. The cutoff now clears only by switching the robot off and on.

problems.what: No code anywhere in the firmware drove a relay. IO14 was declared as an emergency SENSE input while the hardware uses it to switch the contactor.
problems.impact: The coil was never energized, so the motor rails were never powered, so the pack - which sits behind the relay - read 0 V and could not be measured at all. The visible symptom was that the relay never clicked.

tasks.title: Confirm which pin the relay/mushroom sense actually lands on

tasks.title: INA address map does not match the built hardware
tasks.test: with the relay closed, the pack rails must be the two INAs reading 11-12 V
tasks.result: 0x45 is the fan as configured, but the other 5 V rail is the processor at 0x41 - power.h calls 0x41 MOTOR A and 0x40 processor, so those two are swapped. Left alone until the relay is closed and it can be read off the hardware rather than inferred.
